title: The map that traced a killer to a water pump
summary: In 1854 physician John Snow linked a London cholera outbreak to one water pump, at a time when most doctors blamed 'bad air'. The popular story leaves out that the outbreak was already fading.

scenes.text: In 1854, a map helped trace a deadly outbreak — and changed medicine.
Cholera was killing hundreds in Soho, London. Most doctors blamed 'miasma': bad air.
Physician John Snow suspected the water.

items.title: Mapped the deaths
items.detail: They clustered around one pump on Broad Street

items.title: Checked the exceptions
items.detail: Nearby brewery workers, who drank beer, were largely spared

items.title: Acted
items.detail: Persuaded officials to remove the pump handle

scenes.text: Here's the part the legend often skips.
scenes.reveal: The outbreak was already declining when the handle came off.

scenes.text: His real legacy: using careful data to find a cause — a foundation of modern epidemiology.
Evidence can beat even the most widely held assumption.

sources.title: On the Mode of Communication of Cholera (2nd ed.)
